texts.preamble: Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.5084/2023 Kabc0B0114522023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 27th Day of January-2025 M.V.C. No.5084/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Smt. A. Eswaramma
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 17.07.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.07.2023 at about 08.15 a.m., petitioner was walking on the side of the road, carefully, observing all traffic rules, proceeding near Apollo Pharmacy, 13th Cross, Basavanapura Main Road, Bangalore, at that time rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556 rode the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 48 years, the petitioner was working as Attender at Cambridge College and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do her job and hence lost her earnings. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/ 2 motorcycle. Further, this respondent seeks protection U/s 134(c), 156(6) of M. V. Act. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, the negligence is on the part of the petitioner only. Further, this respondent proceeded towards the jurisdictional police station, reported the incident and they refused to take the complaint of the rider/owner of the motorcycle.
texts.arguments: Further this respondent submits that, as per the police documents the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of the petitioner as she was crossing the road where there is no zebra crossing lines. Further this respondent submits that, the rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and owner knowing fully has entrusted the said vehicle to him. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the petitioner attempted to cross the main road where there is no Zebra crossing and without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed the offending motorcycle. Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 18. The learned counsel for petitioner submits that, the accident is caused due to sole negligence of respondent No.2 i.e., rider of offending vehicle. Hence, he argued that, both respondents are liable to pay compensation. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 argued that, the accident was caused due to the negligent act of the petitioner. Further he argued that, the petitioner was crossing the road at there was no Zebra crossing and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner also and he submitted that, consider 25% negligence on the part of petitioner. In support of his line of argument he relied upon the following decisions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, i.e., MFA NO. 1192/2018 between Thippeshappa and others And M.D, KSRTC and another, MFA NO.2259/2013 C/w MFA NO.4572/2018 between M.D, KSRTC And Sri. Parameshwar C. Aralaguppi and another. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Attender in Cambridge Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/ 6 College and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, in support of her claim she has produced the Resignation Letter at Ex.P.15. The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, she is still working at Cambridge college as Attender. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
